statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the minimum possible total Manhattan distance: defining C(f) = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (|workers[i][0] - bikes[f(i)][0]| + |workers[i][1] - bikes[f(i)][1]|) for an injective function f : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,m-1}, there exists an injective f with C(f) = r, and for every injective g : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,m-1}, C(g) >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} min_{0 <= j < m} (|workers[i][0] - bikes[j][0]| + |workers[i][1] - bikes[j][1]|).
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (|workers[i][0] - bikes[i][0]| + |workers[i][1] - bikes[i][1]|).
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if there exists an injective function f : {0,...,n-1} -> {0,...,m-1} such that for every i with 0 <= i < n, workers[i][0] = bikes[f(i)][0] and workers[i][1] = bikes[f(i)][1] (equivalently, the Manhattan distance between workers[i] and bikes[f(i)] is 0).
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and for every permutation π of {0,...,n-1}, letting workers'[i] = workers[π(i)] for 0 <= i < n, the function on (workers', bikes) also returns r.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and for every permutation σ of {0,...,m-1}, letting bikes'[j] = bikes[σ(j)] for 0 <= j < m, the function on (workers, bikes') also returns r.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and for every pair of integers (dx, dy) with 0 <= workers[i][0]+dx < 1000 and 0 <= workers[i][1]+dy < 1000 for all i, and 0 <= bikes[j][0]+dx < 1000 and 0 <= bikes[j][1]+dy < 1000 for all j, letting workers'[i] = [workers[i][0]+dx, workers[i][1]+dy] and bikes'[j] = [bikes[j][0]+dx, bikes[j][1]+dy], the function on (workers', bikes') also returns r.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and letting workers'[i] = [999 - workers[i][0], workers[i][1]] and bikes'[j] = [999 - bikes[j][0], bikes[j][1]], the function on (workers', bikes') also returns r.
preconditions: Let n = len(workers) and m = len(bikes). Assume 1 <= n <= m <= 10; every workers[i] and bikes[j] has length 2; all coordinates are integers in [0, 1000); all workers are pairwise distinct; all bikes are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and letting workers'[i] = [workers[i][0], 999 - workers[i][1]] and bikes'[j] = [bikes[j][0], 999 - bikes[j][1]], the function on (workers', bikes') also returns r.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and letting workers'[i] = [workers[i][1], workers[i][0]] and bikes'[j] = [bikes[j][1], bikes[j][0]], the function on (workers', bikes') also returns r.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r. If m < 10, then for every coordinate [x, y] with 0 <= x < 1000, 0 <= y < 1000 not equal to any bikes[j], letting bikes' be the list obtained by appending [x, y] to bikes, the function on (workers, bikes') returns a result r' with r' <= r.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and assuming n < m, for every coordinate [x, y] with 0 <= x < 1000, 0 <= y < 1000 not equal to any workers[i], letting workers' be the list obtained by appending [x, y] to workers, the function on (workers', bikes) returns a result r' with r' >= r.

statement: The function on (workers, bikes) returns a result r, and for every positive integer k such that k * c < 1000 for every coordinate c appearing in workers or bikes, letting workers'[i] = [k * workers[i][0], k * workers[i][1]] and bikes'[j] = [k * bikes[j][0], k * bikes[j][1]], the function on (workers', bikes') returns a result r' with r' = k * r.
